`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```

`/api/v1/responses` is stateless: tell it your codename in one request and it does not know in
the next, and the ~3,173 baseline tokens are the tool harness rather than your history.
`conversation_id` is documented "pass-through only, not forwarded to the LLM provider", so it
is observability. There is no memory or vault path anywhere in the API's 181.

That is because the memory engine ships in `anuma-ai/sdk` as client-side code. `src/lib/memory/`
holds fact extraction, decay with per-type TTLs, reciprocal-rank fusion, maximal marginal
relevance, entity salience, graph traversal, topic extraction, consolidation and reflection,
over a local encrypted vault (`src/lib/db/memoryVault/`). `assembleMemoryContext()` reads that
vault and builds the prompt **before** the request is sent. The server never holds your history,
which is the point of a private AI layer.

So a client that wants memory has to implement it rather than call it. This server does not yet:
what it offers instead is multi-turn, where the caller resends the conversation.

```jsonc
{ "model": "...", "messages": [
  { "role": "user", "text": "My project codename is Kestrel." },
  { "role": "assistant", "text": "Noted, Kestrel." },
  { "role": "user", "text": "What is my project codename?" } ] }
```
